newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts to charge higher to 116-13.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts to charge higher to 116-13.

text.p: September gilt futures on LIFFE have crossed over a key barrier, securing the opportunity for a trouble-free rise to at least 116-13 on Thursday, technical analysts said.

Bob Emanuels, vice president at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett in Amsterdam, said Wednesday's break through 115-00 was encouraging since it confirmed a rising triangle in a 30-minute chart that formed over the last two days.
"There is no sign of danger here...it means that on the upside the potential is at least another 20 basis points," Emanuels said. At 0700 GMT, Sept gilts were up 5/32 at 115-23.
Emanuels said on a longer term outlook, the target for gilts was 117-00 in the next six to eight weeks.
This bullish view would not be negated until levels below 113-24 were seen, he said. This is the low on July 3 and the bottom of a congestion area.
Before 113-24, more important support would be provided by an upsloping support line which comes in at around 114-12 on Thursday. But Emanuels did not expect this to be tested.
"I wouldn't focus on the downside. I would use short term corrections to adjust my position," he said.

Hans Guenter Redeker, senior economist at Chase in London said the break above 115-05 was significant, creating the potential to rise to 116-02, the upper boundary of a trend channel on the daily chart.

"Correction here would be limited," he said, adding the market had a chance of forming a runaway gap with further upside implications. A close above 116-02 would signal further gains to 117-25 and the 121-01 level traded in December 1993.
"Technically the market is in the same position as the Italian market in 1995 when there was a big rise," he said, adding that the long term target for gilts was 124-00/126-00.
Redeker saw support at 115-03/05 which is also solidified by a gap between 115-02 and 115-07 formed at the open on Wednesday.
Gilts, taking their cue from rallying T-bonds, jumped to a contract high of 115-25 on Wednesday, a gain of 27 basis points on the day, but finished below there at 115-18.
At the short end, December short sterling stood 0.02 up on Thursday at 92.65.
